classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate each quadratic twice and explain how the constant second derivative determines concavity for every real x.

content.prompt: A curve is concave up when $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}>0$ and concave down when $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}<0$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Explain why $y=x^2-3x+7$ is concave up for all values of $x$.

answer.short: $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=2>0$ for all $x$, so the curve is concave up for all values of $x$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=2x-3\\\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=2\end{align*}$$
Since $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=2>0$ for all $x$, the curve is concave up for all values of $x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why $y=-3x^2+2x-4$ is concave down for all values of $x$.

answer.short: $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-6<0$ for all $x$, so the curve is concave down for all values of $x$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=-6x+2\\\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=-6\end{align*}$$
Since $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-6<0$ for all $x$, the curve is concave down for all values of $x$.
